title: Canary: the Gate G2 loss curve still reproduces at HEAD
hypothesis: Re-running the Gate G2 loss-curve experiment at HEAD regenerates the committed loss-curve.summary.csv. If it does not, a code change altered a seeded stream or the training numerics, and every number produced after that change is on a different stream from every number before it.

config.freeze: none: both world models train on every step

decisionRule.text: Pass if the regenerated loss-curve.summary.csv has the same rows and columns as the committed reference and every numeric cell is within maxDifference of it, where the difference between a and b is |a - b| / max(1, |a|, |b|). A maxDifference of 0 means byte-identical. A NaN halt is a fail.

onFail: Find the commit that changed the stream: git bisect with `npm run exp -- 0000 --scratch --require-pass`. If the change was intended, say so in the PR that makes it and add a new canary card with a new reference. Do not edit this card or its reference.
